chunks: Abul Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Abdullah al-Musawi al-Alawi narrated to me from Abdullah ibn Nahik, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn Hakam, from Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: There is a grave near you to which no anguished person goes without Allah removing his anguish and fulfilling his requests.

key_terms.مَكْرُوبٌ: one who is anguished or distressed

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual benefit of visiting the grave mentioned in this hadith from Kamil al-Ziyarat?
ai.summary: In Kamil al-Ziyarat, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) identifying a specific grave, widely understood by Shia scholars to be that of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.), as a locus of divine relief for the distressed. This narration underscores the metaphysical reality of the Ahl al-Bayt’s intercessory power, where physical visitation serves as a conduit for Allah to remove calamities and fulfill the needs of the believer, reinforcing the concept of 'tawassul' through the Imams.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 1. Abul Qāsim Ja’far ibn Muḥammad ibn Ibrāhīm ibn ‘Abdillāh Al-Mūsawi Al-‘Alawi narrated to me from ‘Abdillāh ibn Nahīk, from Ibn Abī ‘Umayr, from Hishām ibn Ḥakam, from Fuďayl ibn Yasār, who said:
Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: There is a grave near you to which no anguished person goes without Allāh removing his anguish and fulfilling his requests.
